title: Light-mediated Formation and Patterning of Hydrogels for Cell Culture Applications
protocol: Synthesize pendant peptides (Pep1Alloc, AF488Pep1Alloc) by standard solid phase peptide synthesis techniques.
Synthesize crosslinking peptides (Pep2Alloc) by standard solid phase peptide synthesis techniques.
Synthesize thiol-functionalized polymer by a three-step procedure for end group modification.
Purchase PEG4SH (Mn ~ 20 kDa), Pep1Alloc, and Pep2Alloc commercially if desired.
Synthesize the photoinitiator (LAP) by a two-step reaction as described in literature.
Dry all glassware in an oven for more than 2 hours at 80 °C.
Add a stir bar to an empty single-neck round-bottom flask (100 ml).
Cover the flask with a septum and secure it on top of a magnetic stirring hot plate.
Insert a needle through the septum, leaving its outer end open to the atmosphere.
Attach a second needle to an inert gas line and purge the flask for 10-15 minutes with inert gas.
Turn on the stir plate at medium speed carefully after adding dimethyl phenylphosphonite to avoid splashing.
Add 1.6 g (~1.46 ml) 2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl chloride dropwise to the flask containing dimethyl phenylphosphonite using a syringe with a needle to pierce the septum.
Cover the reaction vessel with foil and stir for 18 hr under argon or nitrogen.
Raise the height of the flask, place an oil bath on the stirrer, and lower the flask into the oil bath.
Heat the bath and the flask to 50 °C while maintaining magnetic stirring.
Dissolve 3.05 g lithium bromide in 50 ml of 2-butanone.
Raise the flask out of the oil bath and add the lithium bromide solution to the round-bottom flask, removing the septum briefly.
Seal the flask again with the septum and lower it back into heated oil bath.
Allow the reaction to proceed for 10 min at 50 °C.
Turn off argon, remove the flask from heat, and allow the mixture to rest for 4 hr under foil cover.
Pour product into a glass frit funnel or funnel lined with appropriate filter paper.
Rinse filtrate three times with 50 ml of 2-butanone.
Reconstitute Pep1Alloc by weighing the total mass and dissolving in sterile PBS containing 1% penicillin/streptomycin and 0.5 μg/ml fungizone.
Reconstitute Pep2Alloc by weighing the total mass and dissolving in sterile PBS containing 1% penicillin/streptomycin and 0.5 μg/ml fungizone.
Mix Pep1Alloc and Pep2Alloc stocks to achieve gels with final moduli relevant for soft tissue applications (Young's modulus ~ 0.5-5 kPa).
Aliquot mixed gel solution and store at -20 °C until use.
Weigh PEG4SH into a sterile microcentrifuge tube and dissolve in PBS containing 1% penicillin/streptomycin and 0.5 μg/ml fungizone.
Dissolve LAP into a sterile microcentrifuge tube using PBS containing 1% penicillin/streptomycin and 0.5 μg/ml fungizone to a final concentration of 7.5 mg/ml.
Cut the tips off of 1 ml syringes using a razor blade.
Remove plungers from the syringe shafts.
Submerge syringe shafts and plungers in 70% ethanol for 15 min.
Place syringe shafts and plungers in a sterile cell culture hood to dry for 30 min.
Push out any excess drops of ethanol inside syringe shafts using the plunger.
Soak glass slides and rubber gaskets in 70% ethanol for 15 min.
Place soaked materials in sterile cell culture hood to dry.
Coat half of the sterilized slides with anti-adhesive coating as directed by manufacturer.
Calibrate the lamp for syringe or glass slide molds.
Attach a collimating lens to the end of the liquid-filled light guide.
Adjust distance of the light guide from samples to achieve desired spot size.
Place cut syringe mold in microcentrifuge tube holder.
Hold radiometer at height of syringe tip where samples will be held.
Adjust shutter percentage to achieve a light intensity of 10 mW/cm² at 365 nm.
Place a glass slide mold onto a sterile surface.
Hold the radiometer detector at the height of the glass slide mold.
Adjust shutter settings to achieve a light intensity of 10 mW/cm2 at 365 nm.
Record the adjusted shutter settings for future use.
Mix stock solutions of PEG4SH, Pep2Alloc, Pep1Alloc, LAP, and PBS+PS+FZ according to spreadsheet calculations.
Pipette the resulting gel precursor solution vigorously to ensure even mixing.
Prepare thick hydrogels by pipetting 10-20 µl of the gel precursor solution into the tip of a sterile, cut syringe.
Make a single gel per syringe with a thickness of approximately 0.5-1.5 mm based on volume and syringe diameter.
Place the rubber gasket around the edges of the non-coated glass slide.
Pipette 5-10 µl gel precursor solution onto the non-coated glass slide.
Place the glass slide coated with anti-adhesive on top of the gel solution.
Secure the glass slides with small binder clips to stabilize.
Measure lamp intensity to achieve 10 mW/cm2 at the gel surface.
Apply light for 1 to 5 min to allow complete polymerization of gels.
Use a shorter polymerization time (1 min) for gels with higher PEG4SH content (8 wt% or greater).
Use a longer polymerization time (3-5 min) for gels with lower PEG4SH content (5-8 wt%) to produce fully-polymerized hydrogels.
Place gels from syringe tip molds into a sterile non-treated 48-well plate.
Place glass slides into a sterile dish.
Rinse gels 3 x 15 min with cell culture medium or appropriate buffer.
Mix stock solutions of PEG4SH, Pep2Alloc, LAP, and PBS+PS+FZ according to the spreadsheet calculation.
Leave free thiols in the range of 0.2-5 mM for later reaction with Pep1Alloc.
Pipette the precursor solution vigorously to ensure even mixing of the solution.
Prepare thick and thin hydrogels as laid out in steps 2.1.2 to 2.1.6.
Do not place gels in growth medium prior to photopatterning.
Cover pre-formed gels with Pep1Alloc/LAP solution and incubate for 1 hr at 37 °C.
Remove excess Pep1Alloc/LAP solution after incubation.
If gels were molded in a syringe tip, use a spatula to carefully transfer the gels from the 48-well plate to a sterile glass slide for patterning.
Place a photomask with the desired pattern directly on top of syringe- and glass slide-molded gels.
Ensure that the printed part of the mask touches the gel for optimal pattern fidelity.
Place samples under the lamp and irradiate for 1 min with the lamp settings used for glass slides.
Place syringe-molded gels into a sterile, 48-well non-tissue culture treated plate.
Place glass slide-molded gels adhered to the glass slides into a sterile dish.
Rinse gels 3 times for 15 minutes each with cell culture medium or appropriate buffer.
Prepare Ellman's reaction buffer by dissolving 2.4 g sodium phosphate dibasic and 74.4 mg EDTA in 200 ml dIH2O.
Adjust the pH of Ellman's reaction buffer to 7.5-8 using NaOH or phosphoric acid solutions.
Dissolve 5.27 mg cysteine in 15 ml reaction buffer to prepare the cysteine working solution.
Dilute cysteine working solution in reaction buffer to create standards with final concentrations of 2, 1.5, 1.25, 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25, and 0 mM cysteine.
Dissolve 4 mg Ellman's reagent in 1 ml reaction buffer to prepare the Ellman's reagent solution.
Sonicate Ellman's reagent solution to completely dissolve the reagent.
Quantify the concentration of free thiols in gels using Ellman's assay.
Determine the swollen gel volume of 'thin' 5 µl gels based on the volumetric swelling ratio, Q.
Make three 20 µl 'thick' gels using syringe molds.
Place gels in Ellman's reaction buffer for 24 hours.
Subsequently weigh the equilibrium swollen mass of thick gels (MS).
Lyophilize the gels and subsequently weigh the dry mass (MD) of thick gels.
Calculate the volumetric swelling ratio by Q = 1 + ρpolymer/ρsolvent(MS/MD-1), where ρpolymer is 1.07 g/cm3 for PEG, ρsolvent is 1.0 g/cm3 for PBS/H2O.

Calculate the theoretical dry mass of a 5 µl 'thin' gel to be used for Ellman's Assay by summing the masses of individual components PEG4SH, Pep1Alloc, and Pep2Alloc (MD = MPEG4SH + MPep1Alloc + MPep2Alloc).
Form thin hydrogels for patterning as described in section 2.2 (5 µl volume).
Make gels with excess free thiols and pattern half of these samples with Pep1Alloc using a clear coverslip to flood expose the entire gel with light.
Perform quantitative Ellman's assay based on the calculated swollen mass MS for the 'thin' gel.
Place 'patterned' and non-'patterned' gels in wells of a 48-well plate.
Rinse the gels 3 times for 15 minutes each with Ellman's reaction buffer to allow unreacted species to diffuse out and equilibrium swelling to occur.
Add extra Ellman's reaction buffer to the rinsed gels so that the total volume is a multiple of 20 µl.
Pipette cysteine standards into individual wells (not containing gels) of a 96-well plate in multiples of 20 µl based on the volume used in the previous step.
Dilute Ellman's reagent in reaction buffer by mixing multiples of 180 µl reaction buffer with 3.6 µl Ellman's reagent.
Add diluted Ellman's reagent to wells containing standards and samples.
For 20 μl samples, add 183.6 μl solution to each well.
Double this amount of diluted Ellman's reagent for 40 μl samples (or scale accordingly based on the size of the sample).
Incubate or place on a shaker for 1 hr and 30 min at room temperature.
Take 100 μl of solution from samples and standards.
Place into wells of a 96-well plate.
Read absorbance at 405 nm on a plate reader.
Plot the standard curve (absorbance versus concentration).
Fit a linear function to the standard curve.
Calculate the concentration of free thiols in the 'diluted gel' solution based on absorbance readings.
Determine the free thiol concentration in the gels without reaction buffer, taking into account the dilution with reaction buffer.
Soak thin hydrogels patterned with Pep1Alloc in Ellman's reaction buffer for 1 hr.
Remove excess reaction buffer by gently wiping around the edges of the hydrogel with a tissue.
Pipette Ellman's reagent directly on the surface of the gel.
Immediately image the gel on a light microscope at 10X or stereomicroscope with a color camera.
Image gels immediately to capture visualization patterns, which will dissipate within 5 minutes.
For higher resolution or three-dimensional visualization, photopattern AF488-modified Pep1Alloc (or similar fluorescent peptide) onto the gel.
Image the pattern on a fluorescent microscope.
Use a confocal microscope to take z-stack images of the gel for x-, y-, and z-plane observation.
Store gels containing fluorescent peptides in a container wrapped in foil at 4 °C to protect from light.
Trypsinize cells from plates according to standard sterile mammalian cell culture procedures.
Quench the trypsin with growth medium after detachment occurs.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or other counting device from aliquots of the trypsinized cell suspension (minimum 100 cells).
Centrifuge the bulk cell suspension at 90-110 x g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in PBS or growth medium if the initial suspension is too dilute and recount.
Aliquot portions of resuspended cells into microcentrifuge tubes to achieve a concentration of 5,000 cells/µl when mixed with gel solution.
Centrifuge cell/PBS aliquots at 90-110 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate PBS from cell pellet in microcentrifuge tube right before encapsulation.
Suspend pelleted cells in PEG4SH, Pep2Alloc, Pep1Alloc, LAP, and PBS+PS+FZ to a final concentration of 5,000 cells/μl.
Mold and polymerize hydrogels as described in steps 2.1.2 to 2.1.6.
Place glass slide molds in sterile PBS or growth medium after polymerization to wet the gasket and hydrogel, making it easier to remove the top slide.
Use syringe molds to prevent shear forces that can cause cell death during gel removal.
Rinse gels 3 x 10 min in growth medium to remove unreacted species and excess LAP.
Incubate gels in growth medium at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until the desired time point for further analysis.
Replenish medium every 48 hr or as determined for the application (e.g., typical feeding interval for specific cell type and medium).
Suspend pelleted cells in PEG4SH, Pep2Alloc, LAP, and PBS+PS+FZ to a final concentration of 5,000 cells/µl.
Rinse gels 3 x 10 min in growth medium after patterning to remove unreacted species and excess LAP.
Incubate gels in growth medium at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until the desired time point for further analysis.
Replenish medium every 48 hr or as determined for the application.
Remove growth medium from gels and rinse 3 x 15 min with PBS to allow diffusion of medium from gels.
Thaw live/dead cytotoxicity assay solutions (ethidium homodimer-1 and calcein AM).
Add 2 μl of the 2 mM ethidium homodimer-1 solution to 1 ml sterile PBS.
Add 0.5 μl of the 4 mM calcein AM solution to 1 ml sterile PBS.
Vortex to ensure complete mixing.
Add 300 μl of staining solution to each syringe mold gel in a 48-well plate or enough to cover the surface of gel on a glass slide in a sterile dish.
Incubate for 45 min.
Remove excess staining solution.
Rinse with PBS (3 x 15 min) to remove excess dye from the gels.
Image the gels on a confocal microscope (z-stack images) or an epi-fluorescence microscope at 10X and 488/525 nm Ex/Em.
Quantify viable cells by projecting z-stacks and counting live (green throughout cell body) and dead (red nuclei) cells with imaging software.
Perform metabolic activity assay to determine cell activity post-encapsulation.
Feed encapsulated cells with fresh growth medium 24 hours prior to the assay.
Add MTS reagent solution to each well (20 μl per 100 μl growth medium).
Incubate samples for 1-4 hr at 37 °C and 5% CO2, according to manufacturer's instructions.
Incubate cells sufficiently for MTS reduction and formazan product diffusion out of the gel.
Pipette 100 µl of reduced MTS/Medium into clean wells of a 96-well plate.
Record absorbance at 490 nm on a plate reader.
Subtract background absorbance from sample absorbance values to generate baselined absorbance values.
